summary: # CLO 2025.1 - Materials & Rendering ## Introduction to Materials and Rendering Updates This video introduces the materials and the related updates of the rendering through our new part of the storage function. You can now save the selected version and material as a clothing file in ZPLC format for storage rather than storing the entire project. ## Saving Versions in the 2D Window To save a version, choose the version to be stored in the 2D window. Find the storage in the file, click on "Clothing," select, enter the file name, and click "Save." Let's repeat the above operations to store the hat version. You can see that the clothing file just saved has been stored separately. ## Simplified Storage Process I will show you how to save and store the clothes. Previously, users had to manually delete unnecessary elements before storing. Now, you can only save the necessary parts to simplify the work process. At the same time, it is not interrupted when continuing to process the complete file. This is especially beneficial for creating reusable assets, making it more convenient to use when the version and clothing assets are stored, thereby improving the efficiency of the project. ## Enhanced Rendering Features The new version improves the surface of all print cloths, making them look more harmonious. It can present a more accurate lighting pattern and shadow effect after rendering. To add print to the fabric, select the fabric and click "Add Print." ## Unified Fabric and Print Patterns In the default state, the fabric pattern and the print pattern use two types of stickers. If you want to use the same sticker pattern for both the print cloth and the fabric pattern, you can select the same pattern in the attribute editor. This function is also applicable for transparency, allowing you to select the same pattern for both the print cloth and the fabric pattern in the attribute editor. The fabric pattern and print cloth can use the same PBR sticker pattern, which allows you to present all design elements with a unified light and texture effect. This is a perfect choice for designers who pursue high precision and detail. ## Improvements in Print Cloth Rendering In the previous hollow version, the contrast ratio of the print cloth and the fabric could lead to visual errors. The new version has increased the accurate control of the key print parameters, and the print cloth provides a truly clear presentation of the print effect, which significantly improves readability and accuracy. To activate Print Cloth Render, you can see an additional information prompt next to the print cloth. Zoom in to check the details of the print cloth. Navigate to the attribute editor of the print cloth. ## Adjusting Print Cloth Parameters Using the double needle print cloth as an example, you can see an additional part-time model ratio below. Activate it and set the following print cloth parameters to adjust the effect of the original print cloth pattern percentage: - **Length:** Adjust the length of the needle. - **Position:** Assign the position of the thumb and right finger of the pin. - **Penetration:** Set the penetration pressure. - **Measured Frequency:** Set to the minimum at the bottom in the allotment pattern. You can see the changes in the settings, adjusting the distance between the name line and the edge of the applied line to control the visual thickness of the real line. Set the width of the name line, noting that this parameter is more suitable for name lines with width, such as the edge of the left-hand side. Switch to the name line of the applied line to demonstrate. Adjust the distance between the name line and the edge of the applied line and set multiple name lines. Change back to the double-edged name line display. All changes are only visible when the model image rendering is active and will not affect the parameters of the actual name line itself. After closing the model image rendering, all content will return to the normal view. ## Self-Defined Viewing Pin Images In the previous version, when opening the self-defined viewing pin image, you could only output the self-defined viewing pin image of each color and could not pin the color of a specific viewing. In the 2025.1 version, you can choose the self-defined viewing based on the color of the desired viewing pin image. Open the rendering window and in the image attribute settings, change the viewing period to the self-defined viewing. At this time, the color is current. You can see the following storage settings. In the settings, there will be a selection of the self-defined viewing pin image. Open the selection to render and it will output the color of the flag pin image under the self-defined viewing. ## Combining Flag Rendering Images You can keep the viewing setting as the self-defined viewing and change the color of the flag from the current flag to the full flag. You can also click on the self-defined color you want to choose on the right side. When you choose more than one flag, there will be a flag pin image option at the bottom, and an option to select the self-defined viewing angle has been added. This means that in addition to the self-defined viewing pin image of each flag, you can also combine the flag rendering image of a selected viewing angle. For example, if you choose viewing angle 5 here, after completing the settings, click on the final rendering image. You will get the self-defined viewing angle pin image of each flag and the color pin image under the selected viewing angle. ## Conclusion Based on this update, users can more freely combine the color rendering image of the self-defined viewing angle, which increases the efficiency of work.
